household.name: stool
household.title: stool
household.reason: Wooden stool with a figural handle carved as a human head and incised geometric patterns on the seat, a typical form of household furniture attributed to the Bobo of Mali; the museum notes "probably" as attribution but no conflicting evidence is given.

household.name: stool
household.title: stool
household.reason: A wooden three-legged stool with a carved handle in the form of a human head is a classic Bobo household object; the museum attributes it to Bobo (probably), which counts as adequate evidence.

household.name: stool
household.title: stool
household.reason: A wooden four-legged stool with a carved human/animal-head handle and incised geometric patterns, a classic Bobo-style household seat form; attribution is "probably" but this is a typical Bobo type with no conflicting evidence.

household.name: pall
household.title: pall
household.reason: A single-piece carved wooden yoke/shoulder pall ("bärs hakad över ena axeln" - worn hooked over one shoulder), collected in Bomborokuy, Cercle de Nouna, Burkina Faso, in a family's possession for three generations—consistent with Bobo material culture of the region.

masks-ritual.name: Mask
masks-ritual.title: Ram Mask (Bolo)
masks-ritual.reason: The mask is a classic wooden ram-horned face mask attributed to Bobo blacksmith-carvers of Burkina Faso, used in ritual masquerades — consistent with the claimed culture and category (note: museum says Burkina Faso, not Mali, but the ethnic attribution to Bobo stands).

masks-ritual.name: mask
masks-ritual.title: mask
masks-ritual.reason: The elongated plank mask with two stacked faces, carved bird-head crest row, and geometric painted patterns (white, brown, red) is a classic Bobo (Bwa-related) plank mask form from Burkina Faso, matching the museum's own note ("bobo fing"); the "Mali" claim is likely a geographic slip but the Bobo/Bwa ethnic attribution and object type are sound.

masks-ritual.name: mask, Bougou Dinde
masks-ritual.title: mask, Bougou Dinde
masks-ritual.reason: This is a wooden plank/"butterfly" mask with a carved human face and wings decorated in geometric triangle, checkerboard and diamond patterns in black, white and red — the classic style of Bwa/Bobo plank masks from Burkina Faso, matching the claimed Bobo origin and location.

masks-ritual.name: Hjälmmask, mask
masks-ritual.title: Hjälmmask, mask
masks-ritual.reason: A wooden helmet mask carved as an animal head (ram/antelope with curved ribbed horns), described as a mask for the protective spirit "Do" worn during Bobo funerary and fertility rites near Bobo-Dioulasso — a classic Bobo ritual mask type.

sculpture.name: skulptur, miniatyr, figur, sculpture
sculpture.title: skulptur, miniatyr, figur, sculpture
sculpture.reason: A small bronze/copper anthropomorphic figure acquired in Bobo-Dioulasso and explicitly attributed to the Bobo Fing people, wearing a conical hat and carrying a tool over the shoulder — a maker-culture-attested object consistent with the claimed ethnicity.

sculpture.name: skulptur, sculpture
sculpture.title: skulptur, sculpture
sculpture.reason: A carved wooden standing figure with simplified facial features, collected in Bomborokuy, Burkina Faso, and purchased locally — consistent with Bobo figurative sculpture used in ritual/shrine contexts.

sculpture.name: skulptur, miniatyr, figur, sculpture
sculpture.title: skulptur, miniatyr, figur, sculpture
sculpture.reason: A cast metal crocodile figurine, acquired in the town of Bobo-Dioulasso and attributed to the Bobo Fing people per museum records; crocodile figures are a known cast-metal ornament type in this Mali/Burkina region.

sculpture.name: skulptur, Träskulptur, sculpture
sculpture.title: skulptur, Träskulptur, sculpture
sculpture.reason: A wooden seated figure carved by a Bobo artisan in Bomborokuy, Burkina Faso, purchased locally in 1974 — consistent with Bobo sculptural tradition.

photo.name: kvinna, fotografi, photograph
photo.title: kvinna, fotografi, photograph
photo.reason: A 1958 documentary photograph in Bobo-Dioulasso showing two women in printed dresses in front of a Sudano-Sahelian mudbrick building, consistent with Bobo daily life and vernacular architecture in the region.

instruments.name: trumma
instruments.title: trumma
instruments.reason: A tall skin-and-wood cylindrical drum with cord lacing, collected in Bomborokuy, Burkina Faso, and attributed to the Bobo (Bobo Ule) ethnic group — consistent with regional drum types made and used by this people.

instruments.name: trumma
instruments.title: trumma
instruments.reason: A laced hourglass-shaped skin-and-wood drum collected at Bomborokuy, Upper Volta, attributed to the Bobo (Bobo Ule) ethnic group — a traditional membranophone consistent with the claimed maker and origin.

instruments.name: trumma
instruments.title: trumma
instruments.reason: A cylindrical wood-and-hide hand drum collected from Bomborokuy, Burkina Faso, purchased locally — a plausible traditional instrument type used in this Bobo region.

instruments.name: trumma
instruments.title: trumma
instruments.reason: A cylindrical skin-and-wood drum collected in Bomborokuy, Burkina Faso, played with a drumstick — a musical instrument consistent with Bobo craft and use.
